content.title: About
content.content: The egg salad sandwich on wheat bread is a classic light lunch or snack. Whole‑wheat bread provides a soft, slightly crunchy base, while the egg salad—made from boiled eggs, mayonnaise, mustard, and seasonings—adds a creamy, savory flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg salad became popular in the United States in the early 20th century as a convenient sandwich filling.
Wheat bread is often chosen over white bread for its higher fiber and B‑vitamin content.
Traditional recipes include finely chopped eggs, celery, and dill for extra aroma.
The sandwich packs well in plastic wrap, making it a favorite office lunch.
Variations may add avocado, spinach, or a light yogurt‑based dressing instead of mayo.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Both wheat bread and eggs supply B12, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Mayonnaise or alternative spreads contribute monounsaturated fats that can support heart health in moderation.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Whole‑wheat bread adds dietary fiber, aiding normal digestion.

items.title: Vitamin D and choline
items.content: Eggs are a good source of choline, important for brain function, and contain a modest amount of vitamin D.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from mild to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Mayonnaise and bread add calories; portion control is advisable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, making the sandwich unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. It can be served cold or lightly toasted. Add lettuce, tomato, or cucumber slices for extra freshness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. If the bread begins to dry out, wrap it tightly in plastic. Keep the egg salad separate if you need longer storage.
